Topics · Hard times

Is it shameful to need help as a refugee?

Moses, a refugee, admits his need unashamed. The earth is God's, hosts are praised, the refugee has a right.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ٢٢ وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ ۖ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا ۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ ۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ٢٣ فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ٢٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way." And when he came to the water [i.e., well] of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women holding back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man." So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need."

Quran · Al-Qasas 28:22-24

Translation

But I am poor and needy. May the Lord think about me. You are my help and my deliverer. Don’t delay, my God.

Original · Hebrew

וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֲדֹנָ֪י יַחֲשָׁ֫ב לִ֥י עֶזְרָתִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־תְּאַחַֽר׃

the Psalms · 40:17

World English Bible

The Quran tells of Moses setting out for a land he did not know, saying only that perhaps his Lord would guide him to the right way. At a well he watered the flock for two women, then sat in the shade and said he was in need of whatever good God would send him. He called himself needy without shame, and the text keeps that sentence.

A question for you

What do you need most this week?

If you sayPapers and a place.
ThenThese are real needs and real rights. This page cannot grant them, but it does not look down on you for asking.
If you sayTo be treated as a person.
ThenThat is your due. A later part here speaks of how those who host are to treat you.
If you sayNews of the family I left.
ThenMissing those you left is a pain that has its place. You may hold it here without explaining it.

﴿وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْمَشْرِقُ وَٱلْمَغْرِبُ ۚ فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا۟ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And to Allāh belongs the east and the west. So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face[37] of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

Translator's notes

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:115

Translation

For from the rising of the sun even to its going down, my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense will be offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations,” says Yahweh of Armies.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֣י מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֜מֶשׁ וְעַד־מְבוֹא֗וֹ גָּד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבְכָל־מָק֗וֹם מֻקְטָ֥ר מֻגָּ֛שׁ לִשְׁמִ֖י וּמִנְחָ֣ה טְהוֹרָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

Malachi · 1:11

World English Bible

Land can be taken and a house can be left. This verse says the east and the west belong to God, and wherever you turn there is His face. It does not deny your loss of country. It says there is no border on who sees you. The camp lies under the same sky that stood over your house.

A question for you

The verse ends by calling God vast. What does that word mean to you now?

If you sayA place I cannot be sent out of.
ThenThat is what the verse says about the relationship with God, not about borders and papers.
If you sayTo be heard even when far away.
ThenThat is in the verse too, and in the verses on nearness.
If you sayI feel nothing.
ThenThat is all right. The verse waits and does not hurry.

﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلْإِيمَـٰنَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِى صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةً مِّمَّآ أُوتُوا۟ وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ ۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [also for] those who were settled in the Home [i.e.,al-Madīnah] and [adopted] the faith before them.[1656] They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what they [i.e., the emigrants] were given but give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.

Translator's notes

[1656] Before the settlement of the emigrants (Muhājireen) among the Anṣār, for whom a share is delegated as well.

Quran · Al-Hashr 59:9

Translation

The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

Original · Ancient Greek

δευτέρα αὕτη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν. μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν.

the Gospel (Mark) · 12:31

World English Bible

﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُۥ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allāh [i.e., the Qur’ān]. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:6

Translation

“You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

Original · Hebrew

וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 23:9

World English Bible

The Quran praises people who gave refuge to those who came to them, loved them, and preferred them to themselves even in their own need. It also says that anyone who asks for protection, even from the other side, is to be granted it and then escorted to where they are safe. So your hope is written there: to ask, to be sheltered, to reach safety. The first verse praises those who host; the second commands protection for one who asks. This is more than a favour.

A question for you

What do you need from those who host you?

If you sayTo be treated with dignity.
ThenDignity in the text is for the whole person, and you will not be asked to earn it.
If you sayTo feel safe first.
ThenThe verse puts it in that order: protection, then safety. Everything else follows.
If you sayFor someone to listen.
ThenA fair request. Listening is a form of shelter.

The same in the other books

Translation

If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐάν τις εἴπῃ ὅτι Ἀγαπῶ τὸν θεόν, καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῇ, ψεύστης ἐστίν· ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν ἑώρακεν, τὸν θεὸν ὃν οὐχ ἑώρακεν οὐ δύναται ἀγαπᾶν. καὶ ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔχομεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν θεὸν ἀγαπᾷ καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ.
